sections.title: Creating a queued scan run
sections.what: Checks the chosen scope first. If it is not an enrich-mode scope with at least one project, it refuses and reports the project count. Otherwise it saves a new run marked queued and returns it with the resolved scope.

sections.watch_out: This check is the only thing stopping an empty run from being created, so changes to the scope resolver affect it directly.

summary: Creates a queued reality-scan run for a chosen scope, but only when that scope resolves to existing Yard projects.
purpose: The one place a new scan run is recorded before it is started.
why: The comment says the same path serves the run creation route and the research-import catch-up. The checks stop a run from being queued for an empty selection. Likely reason: avoids wasted runs.
how: 1. Check the chosen scope with the scope resolver, which also decides the scope kind. 2. Reject it unless the mode is enrich and at least one project matches. 3. Save a new run row with status queued. 4. Return the run and the resolved scope so the caller can start it.
inputs: A reality-scan scope describing the industry, segment or project selected.
outputs: The new run row and the resolved scope, or a validation error with a message.
risks: Nothing stops the same scope being queued twice. The pickup step guards against running duplicates at once. A change in the scope resolver directly changes which selections are accepted.
debug: If the user sees a message about zero projects, check that the selection has Yard records. If a queued run never starts, check the server logs for the queued-run pickup.
